note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses), written on 18 Oct 2026 after the device move: the 15-17 Oct round left no record for this item. Not yet acted on.

item-quality.verdict: Mostly sound, but do not accept it until F1 is fixed, together with the compliance decision on v2/v3. What holds up: a competent developer can solve the task from the instruction and the prefilled inspect_graph result with one change_graph call. GRC-Agent's own inspect_graph on start.grc (inspect_start.json) shows that lp_taps.cutoff_freq = cutoff_high, hp_taps.cutoff_freq = cutoff_low, the shared bp_low / bp_high / transition, the FIR comments and every connection. The answer is five update_params entries. The instruction states every number the signal checks use: 48 kHz, 262144 samples after 4096, the file names, float, and each share and RMS with its tolerance. The derived numbers are correct: sqrt(3.75/24) = 0.395, sqrt(16.75/24) = 0.835, sqrt(3.5/24) = 0.382 and sqrt(20.5/24) = 0.924; 90 % slices of 24.0 / 5.3 / 25.7 / 4.3 %; RRC power 1/sps, (1 - 0.25) x 6 kHz and (1 + 0.25) x 6 kHz. The start graph fails f2p only. The family (parameter-tune) and level (L2: 11 functional blocks, filtering) match the proposal. There is no fault leakage. The variable-name trap (cutoff_high feeds the low-pass) comes from the original example and is visible in the graph. The 18 Oct band_fraction fix makes no difference here, because the noise has zero mean. Reference margins: lp 0.0013 % above 4 kHz, 26.8 % slice, RMS 0.389; hp 0.0003 %, 6.0 %, 0.835; bp 99.996 %, 29.8 / 30.0 %, 0.373; br 0.0004 %, 4.77 / 4.94 %, 0.922; rrc 0.497, 74.9 %, 0.011 %. Every valid alternative I wrote passes V6 through the real ladder: Hamming with 250 or 400 Hz; Hann with 250 or 500 Hz; Kaiser 6.76 with 500 Hz; Blackman with 100, 50 or 20 Hz (8073 taps; V5 takes 0.23 s, so there is no liveness risk); cutoffs at 3.6 / 7.4 or 3.9 / 7.1 kHz with 200 Hz; the 'cutoff = passband edge' reading (LP 3.5 kHz, HP 7.5 kHz); and taps written directly into the four FIR filters. All 21 mutants are killed by the check named in their 'breaks'. Problems: F1 (medium) the stated scope 'retune parameter values only: keep the existing blocks and their connections' is not checked, and restructured answers pass; F2 (low) 'leave the RRC filter as it is' and 'keep the noise source' are only partly checked; F3 (low) the verbal slice rule and the stated numbers disagree for steep band-pass designs whose edges sit close to the edges of the guard bands. Scratch evidence: /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-09/ (run_alts.py, run_alts2.py, graphcheck.py, rrc_corr.py, inspect_start.py, results.json and every .grc named below). The task directory was not modified.

findings.claim: The instruction requires 'make the change by retuning parameter values only: keep the existing blocks and their connections'. The 16 Oct oracle policy names this kind of wording ('only change parameter values') as one that needs a structural graph check, but task.json has no oracle.graph_checks. An answer that meets the signal checks by restructuring the graph therefore gets full credit, and the item cannot tell a retune from a redesign. authoring_notes.unchecked_scope_constraint says the sentence is 'structural and not observable by V6', which predates graph_checks.py and is no longer true.
findings.evidence: ./gb ladder <file> --task items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-09/task.json passes each of these at V6 (first_failed null, f2p and p2p true): cx_fft_filter_swap.grc (the low-pass fir_filter_xxx replaced by an fft_filter_xxx with the same taps), cx_bp_cascade_added_block.grc (a second fir_filter_xxx inserted between bp_filter and bandpass_sink and the connection rewired) and cx_hp_dc_blocker_added.grc (a dc_blocker_xx inserted before highpass_sink). With oracle.graph_checks = [same_blocks_as_start] and the task loaded through taskio.load (graphcheck.py), all three fail V6 in group 'main': 'added {fft_filter_xxx: 1}, removed {fir_filter_xxx: 1}', 'added {fir_filter_xxx: 1}' and 'added {dc_blocker_xx: 1}'. The reference, v1, alt_hamming_250, p_near_channel_200 and alt_inline_firdes_nowin still pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add oracle.graph_checks that implement the sentence, in the form chosen for compliance F1: either same_blocks_as_start, or (if adding and removing variables is allowed) block_present {ids: [fir_filter_xxx], min 5, max 5}, {ids: [analog_fastnoise_source_x], min 1, max 1} and {ids: [blocks_file_sink], min 5, max 5}, plus max_functional_blocks {max: 11}. Put them in group 'main' (or p2p). Add the scope to spec_properties, rewrite authoring_notes.unchecked_scope_constraint, and add a restructuring mutant (for example the fft_filter_xxx swap) so the mutation gate exercises the check.

findings.claim: 'Leave the RRC filter as it is' and 'Keep ... the noise source' (described as Gaussian white noise with unit power) are checked only through the RMS levels and two RRC band shares. By construction, the check '75 % of the power below 4.5 kHz' cannot detect any roll-off of 0.25 or less: the flat part then covers 0-4.5 kHz and the share is 4.5/6 = 0.75 whatever alpha is. The 7.5 kHz check also tolerates roll-offs up to about 0.3. Changing the RRC roll-off or tap count, or replacing the Gaussian noise with uniform noise of the same power, therefore passes.
findings.evidence: ./gb ladder passes V6 for cx_rrc_alpha_015.grc (rrc RMS 0.504, 74.6 % below 4.5 kHz, 0.011 % above 7.5 kHz), cx_rrc_alpha_030.grc (0.496, 74.8 %, 0.047 %), cx_rrc_ntaps_88.grc (ntaps 22*sps) and cx_noise_uniform.grc (noise_type GR_UNIFORM with amp 1.7320508; every check passes). The seed is fixed at 0, so every answer that leaves the RRC and the noise source alone produces an rrc output that is bit-identical to the start graph's. rrc_corr.py gives equal_prefix True and corr_ref 1.000000 for the reference, the start graph and alt_hann_500, against corr_ref 0.999259 for alpha 0.3, 0.996344 for alpha 0.15, 0.999910 for ntaps 88 and 0.066 for uniform noise.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a p2p check that the RRC output is unchanged: equal_prefix on point rrc against a few hundred samples (after the skip) of the start graph's rrc output. This is exact, which is what 'unchanged' means, and it runs on the same pinned machine. If exact equality is judged too fragile, use corr_ref with min of about 0.99995 and check it against the variants. Otherwise, reduce the wording to what is checked (the RRC output keeps its level and band).

findings.claim: The instruction defines the edge-slice requirement twice, and the two definitions disagree for band-pass designs whose edges are not at the centres of the guard bands. The prose says 'the 1 kHz slices next to the guard bands must carry at least 90 % of the power a perfectly flat passband would give them'. The stated number is a fixed 25.7 %, computed for a flat passband from 3.75 to 7.25 kHz. Together with RMS 0.38 within 5 %, the numbers reject steep band-pass designs that meet every verbal requirement (only the channel, unity gain, roll-off inside the guard bands) when their edges lie within about 50 Hz of a guard-band limit.
findings.evidence: edge_bp_steep_outer.grc (bp_taps at 3550 / 7450 Hz, Blackman, 80 Hz; 99.997 % of the power in 3.5-7.5 kHz) fails V6. Its 4-5 kHz slice is 0.256734 < 0.257, although that is 100.1 % of what a flat 3.55-7.45 kHz passband gives (1/3.9 = 0.2564), and its RMS is 0.4028 > 0.399. edge_bp_steep_inner.grc (3950 / 7050 Hz) fails on RMS, 0.3585 < 0.361. Edges at 3600 / 7400, 3650 / 7350 and 3850 / 7150 Hz pass, as does every plausible design I tried, so the impact is small: the numbers are stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the prose match the numbers: '... at least 90 % of the power they would carry if the passband were perfectly flat with its edges in the middle of the guard bands'. Optionally, also say that each band edge (the -6 dB cutoff) should sit near the middle of its guard band. No oracle change is needed.

compliance.verdict: Compliant on almost every point. One medium finding appears only once the check required by the oracle policy is added. I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates (exit 0, 16 s). Solvability is 10/10, the reference is 968 tokens, all 3 variants pass at V6, the start graph fails at V6 (f2p false, p2p true), and all 21 mutants are valid with a kill rate of 1.0. The rewritten gates.json has the same content as the one written on 18 Oct. Split discipline holds: filter/filter_taps.grc is a dev seed in splits/flowgraph_seed_split.json, and sha256 493f7f19... matches both the split record and source.sha256 (build.py asserts both). The train seed filter/filter_taps_loader.grc is not used, and no signature rule applies to a seed-derived item. id, directory and split agree. cluster_id equals the seed and is unique across items/tier_f. The licence (GPL-3.0-or-later), provenance and review fields are as required. The perturbation record matches the example values that build.py asserts (32000 / 2000 / 14000 / 6000 / 10000 / 1000, sps 2, default alpha, default pool). Every mutation reaches V5 and is killed by the check named in its 'breaks'; I checked each failing check. The tolerances are the stated ones. The canary appears only in task.json. The item is disjoint from reports/reference/training_task_specs.json: no spec covers filter taps, band-reject, guard bands or RRC, and t10 retunes a receiver. The contamination audit's only flag is the generic 8-gram 'at a sample rate of 48 kHz with', shared with a teacher answer. build.py, run in a scratch copy (/home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-09/buildcheck), regenerates task.json, start.grc, reference.grc and all three variants byte-identically. There is no near-duplicate: no other item uses this seed, and gbf-test-03 / gbf-dev-02 share only the style of measuring noise-band power. Findings: F1 (medium) variants v2 and v3 contradict the scope sentence, and with the policy-required check the variants gate fails; F2 (low) ./gb ladder --task cannot evaluate same_blocks_as_start. The task directory was not modified, except that the requested gates re-run rewrote gates.json with identical content.

findings.claim: Two of the three registered variants break the instruction's own scope sentence, so the variants gate passes only because that requirement is not checked. v3_literal_taps_hann deletes five existing blocks (the variables cutoff_low, cutoff_high, bp_low, bp_high and transition), although the instruction says 'keep the existing blocks'. v2_band_plan_variables_kaiser adds three blocks (the variables chan_lo, chan_hi and guard), although it says 'retuning parameter values only'. Once the policy-required structural check is added (item-quality F1), only 1 of 3 variants passes, and the gate needs at least 2.
findings.evidence: graphcheck.py loads the task with taskio.load and sets oracle.graph_checks = [{kind: same_blocks_as_start, group: main}]. The reference and v1_blackman_300hz pass. v2 fails at V6 with main false: 'added {variable: 3}, removed {}'. v3 fails at V6 with main false: 'added {}, removed {variable: 5}'. Its signal groups f2p and p2p stay true.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the wording and the check together. (a) Keep the strict wording and add same_blocks_as_start. Then rewrite v2 to put the band plan in expressions inside the existing variables (for example cutoff_high = '4000 - 500/2', transition = '0.8*500', Kaiser windows). Rewrite v3 to put literal values in the taps blocks while keeping the five scalar variables. Register as a further, genuinely different variant the answer with taps written straight into the four FIR filters (alt_inline_firdes_nowin.grc: taps 'firdes.low_pass(1.0, samp_rate, 3750, 500)' and so on, with the taps variables untouched). It passes V6 and same_blocks_as_start. A window argument must not be written there: 'window.WIN_HAMMING' in a FIR taps field fails V3 because 'window' is not defined (alt_inline_firdes.grc), which is GRC's own behaviour. (b) Or relax the wording to 'keep the noise source, the five FIR filters and the five File Sinks and their connections; adding or removing variables is fine', and check it with block_present counts plus max_functional_blocks 11. That accepts v2 and v3 as they are.

findings.claim: The documented CLI './gb ladder <file> --task task.json' cannot evaluate same_blocks_as_start. ladder.main reads task.json with json.loads and never sets '_dir', so _start_data returns None, and the check fails with 'no start graph' for every answer, including the reference. The gates are not affected, because taskio.load sets _dir. But anyone who uses the CLI to verify the F1 fix for this item, or a reviewer's counter-example, will see the reference rejected. Any runner path that loads task.json directly has the same problem.
findings.evidence: ./gb ladder items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-09/reference.grc --task /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-09/task_with_same_blocks.json exits with 1: first_failed V6, groups {f2p: true, p2p: true, main: false}, graph check detail 'no start graph' (cli_ref_same_blocks.json). The same check passes the reference when the task is loaded through taskio.load (graphcheck.py).
findings.suggested_fix: This is a tool fix outside the task files, for the owner of ladder.py. In ladder.main, set task['_dir'] = str(Path(args.task).resolve().parent), and make sure the Tier-F runner loads tasks through taskio.load. Until then, verify graph checks with ./gb tier-f gates or through taskio.load.
